content: The test image shows a soybean field that is mostly green/healthy, but there are notable pale/white-colored plants visible in the center-upper area. Let me check reference images for the top candidates: Powdery_Mildew and White_Mold.

**Analysis:**

**Test image observations:**
- Soybean field with mostly healthy green plants
- Notable cluster of pale/whitish-gray plants in the center-upper portion of the frame
- The affected plants appear to have a white-to-gray coating covering their foliage
- Surrounding plants remain green and healthy

**Key comparisons:**
- **Powdery Mildew**: Reference shows white-to-gray powdery coating covering entire leaf surfaces — matches the pale/whitish-gray foliage on the affected plants in the test image very well (especially the top-right panel showing gray-covered leaves)
- **White Mold**: Reference shows fluffy white growth on stems, bleached dead stems, brown dead tissue — the test image plants don't show dead/brown necrotic collapse
- **Downy Mildew**: Reference shows pale yellowish spotting with fuzzy undersides — doesn't match the uniform whitish canopy appearance

The white-to-gray appearance of the affected plants, covering the foliage broadly (not individual spots), strongly matches Powdery Mildew where patches coalesce to cover entire leaf surfaces.
